example: Inputs: Distance 300 km, Mileage 18 km/L, Fuel Price ₹105 per litre. Step 1: fuel needed = 300 ÷ 18 = 16.67 litres. Step 2: trip cost = 16.67 × 105 = ₹1,750. Step 3: cost per km = 1,750 ÷ 300 = ₹5.83. Final result: trip cost ₹1,750, needing 16.67 litres of fuel.

formula: Fuel needed (litres) = Distance (km) ÷ Mileage (km/L). Trip Cost = Fuel needed × Fuel Price (₹/L). Cost per km = Trip Cost ÷ Distance.
howTo: Enter the trip length in the Distance (km) field, for example 300.
Enter your vehicle's mileage in the Mileage (km/L) field, for example 18.
Enter the current fuel price in the Fuel Price (₹/L) field, for example 105.
Tap Calculate to see the trip cost.
Read the litres needed and the cost per km shown under the result.
intro: The Fuel Cost Calculator works out how much fuel a trip needs and what it will cost, from the distance, your vehicle's mileage, and the fuel price.
mistakes: Using the maker's claimed mileage instead of your real measured mileage.
Mixing units, such as entering distance in miles while mileage is in km per litre.
Forgetting that city traffic lowers mileage compared with highway driving.
Entering the total fuel price instead of the price per litre.
tips: Measure your mileage over two or three full tanks for a reliable average.
City driving, AC use, and heavy loads all lower real mileage.
Compare the cost per km of two routes or two vehicles to see which is cheaper.
Update the fuel price when it changes — a ₹5 change per litre adds up on long trips.
uses: It is used to budget fuel for a road trip, compare routes, and work out the running cost per kilometre of a vehicle.
